notice: Entirely fictional teaching catalogue. Not real products. No prices, inventory, promotions or expansion announcements are provided.

documents.name: Moon Station
documents.text: Players jointly repair a lunar outpost by routing oxygen and power. Each player has a different engineer role. Moon Station supports 2 to 4 players, takes 25 minutes, and is recommended for ages 8 and up. All players win together by repairing three modules before the oxygen marker reaches zero. Communication is allowed throughout the game. The base box contains 48 repair cards and 12 module tiles. There is no solo mode.

documents.name: Forest Post
documents.text: Players compete to deliver letters along woodland paths. Forest Post supports 3 to 6 players, takes 40 minutes, and is recommended for ages 10 and up. Each completed route earns delivery stamps. The player with the most stamps after six rounds wins; ties are broken by the number of unused bicycle tokens. The base box contains 60 letter cards and 18 bicycle tokens. Forest Post is competitive, not cooperative.

documents.name: Coral Keepers
documents.text: Players jointly restore a reef by placing coral tiles and removing pollution. Coral Keepers supports 1 to 4 players, takes 35 minutes, and is recommended for ages 10 and up. A solo player controls two keeper roles. All players win together when all five reef zones reach health level three. They lose if the pollution bag becomes empty before that objective is met. The base box contains 45 coral tiles and 20 pollution cubes. Communication is unrestricted.

documents.name: Clockwork Market
documents.text: Players compete as merchants buying gears and fulfilling workshop orders. Clockwork Market supports 2 to 5 players, takes 50 minutes, and is recommended for ages 12 and up. At the end of the eighth round, the merchant with the most coins wins. An unfulfilled order costs four coins. Players may trade gears, but may not trade order cards. The base box contains 80 gear tokens and 30 order cards. There is no solo mode.

documents.name: Comet Couriers
documents.text: Players race to deliver parcels between small planets. Comet Couriers supports 2 to 4 players, takes 20 minutes, and is recommended for ages 7 and up. The first player to deliver four parcels wins. A comet shortcut can be used only once per player per game and requires spending two fuel tokens. The base box contains 24 parcel cards and 16 fuel tokens. Comet Couriers is competitive and has no solo mode.

documents.name: Silent Observatory
documents.text: Players jointly assemble star patterns using hidden observation cards. Silent Observatory supports 2 to 5 players, takes 30 minutes, and is recommended for ages 12 and up. During observation rounds, players may not speak or show their cards; each player may place one signal token instead. All players win together by completing four constellations before the sixth round ends. The base box contains 36 observation cards and 10 signal tokens. There is no solo mode.

documents.name: Lantern Duel
documents.text: Two rivals guide lanterns through a shifting maze. Lantern Duel supports exactly 2 players, takes 15 minutes, and is recommended for ages 8 and up. A player wins immediately by lighting all four towers in their own colour. Each turn allows one move and one lantern rotation. Players cannot move through an occupied corridor. The base box contains 16 corridor tiles and 8 lantern pieces. There is no cooperative or solo mode.

documents.name: Festival of Masks
documents.text: Players take hidden roles at a fictional street festival. Festival of Masks supports 6 to 10 players, takes 25 minutes, and is recommended for ages 10 and up. After five voting rounds, the player with the most ribbon tokens wins. Players may discuss and bluff, but may not show their role cards. A tied vote awards no ribbons. The base box contains 20 role cards and 40 ribbon tokens. The game is competitive and requires at least six players.

documents.name: Cloud Rescue
documents.text: Players jointly rescue travellers from floating islands before a storm arrives. Cloud Rescue supports 1 to 5 players, takes 45 minutes, and is recommended for ages 12 and up. A solo player controls three rescue roles. All players win together by rescuing six travellers before the storm track reaches its final space. Each rope bridge may be crossed only twice before it is removed. Communication is unrestricted. The base box contains 18 island tiles and 24 bridge tokens.

documents.name: Pocket Orchard
documents.text: A single player arranges fruit tiles to complete harvest patterns. Pocket Orchard supports exactly 1 player, takes 20 minutes, and is recommended for ages 10 and up. The player wins by completing all three harvest patterns before the draw pile runs out. Fruit tiles may be rotated, but cannot be moved once placed. A wild seed replaces one fruit symbol and can be used only once per game. The base box contains 36 fruit tiles and 6 pattern cards. There is no multiplayer mode.

documents.name: River Racers
documents.text: Players race small boats down a winding river. River Racers supports 2 to 6 players, takes 30 minutes, and is recommended for ages 8 and up. The first boat to cross the finish line wins. Each player may use the waterfall shortcut twice per game, paying three paddle tokens each time. A boat cannot use the shortcut without all three tokens. Boats may share ordinary river spaces. The base box contains 6 boat pieces and 42 paddle tokens. There is no cooperative or solo mode.

documents.name: Ember Archive
documents.text: Players jointly recover records from a fictional underground library. Ember Archive supports 2 to 4 players, takes 50 minutes, and is recommended for ages 14 and up. All players win together by restoring six archive beacons before the heat track reaches twelve. Players may speak freely, but each record card may be exchanged only once. A damaged record requires two repair seals before it can be archived. The base box contains 54 record cards and 30 repair seals. There is no solo mode.
